# ADR112 D7's object key rule as one table of cases. bex-s3 refuses a key that
# breaks it on every route (ValidateKey, lego/backend/internal/objectstorage/
# keys.go), and `bex s3` refuses one before it sends a request
# (keyProblem, lego/cli/internal/s3/location.go). The CLI imports no sibling
# module, so it keeps its own copy of the rule; both modules' tests read this
# file, so the copies cannot drift.
#
# A line is "max-key-bytes N", or "valid" or "invalid" followed by a key
# written as a Go string literal (strconv.Unquote). Each test also tries a key
# of N bytes (valid), one of N+1 bytes (invalid), and one of N/2+1 two-byte
# characters (invalid: the bound counts bytes).

max-key-bytes 1024

# Keys are opaque: dots inside a name, a trailing slash, spaces, escapes and
# Unicode are ordinary.
valid "a"
valid "cat.jpg"
valid "dir/cat.jpg"
valid "a/b/c/d"
valid "with space"
valid "ünï/çödé"
valid "日本語/キー"
valid "trailing/"
valid "dir/"
valid "a.b/c"
valid "dots.in.name"
valid ".hidden"
valid "..hidden"
valid "name.."
valid "a/.../b"
valid "100%"
valid "%2e%2e"
valid "%252e%252e/x"
valid "a?b#c"
valid "a;b"
# Look-alikes of ".." are ordinary names.
valid "．．/x"
valid "‥/x"

invalid ""
invalid "/a"
invalid "/"
invalid "/dbl"
invalid "."
invalid ".."
invalid "../a"
invalid "a/../b"
invalid "x/../y"
invalid "a/.."
invalid "a/./b"
invalid "./a"
invalid "a/."
invalid "a//../b"
invalid "a//b"
invalid "a//"
invalid "dir//file.txt"
invalid "a\\b"
invalid "..\\a"
invalid "a\x00b"
invalid "a\nb"
invalid "a\tb"
invalid "a\x1bb"
invalid "a\x7fb"
invalid "a\xffb"
invalid "a\xe2\x82"
